Day-one retails sales for Grand Theft Auto VI crossed $3.79 billion, and Take-Two sold 32.5 million copies before the game even released.
That game sold an estimated $815 million during its first day on store shelves, a 223 percent increase when accounted for inflation.

GTA VI's $3.79 billion in sales seems well on its way to helping Take-Two hit its projected $3.35-$3.5 billion in net bookings for the fiscal quarter, which will of course be aided by revenue from other games like NBA 2K27 (a game which apparently underperformed because players were holding their breath for GTA VI).
It expects to earn over $8 billion in revenue in full-year 2027 on the back of Rockstar's return to Vice City.

It actually made more than that on the GTA 6 launch day: Rockstar says the game pulled in $3.79 billion in "day one retail sales," making it "the biggest entertainment launch in history."

By way of comparison, Avengers: Endgame, ranked on Wikipedia as the highest grossing movie of all time, earned a little more than $2.9 billion over its entire theatrical run.

Beyond that, I won't even hazard a guess, but consider this: Grand Theft Auto 5, which sold a little over 11 million copies on its launch day in 2013, has now surpassed 230 million copies sold in total.
